en-GB.name: Brim: Fold to Pour
en-GB.subtitle: Fill every glass to the line
en-GB.description:
Your iPhone Duo is the jug.

Lay your Duo open on the table. The top half holds a jug of lemonade. Lift it like a laptop lid and the jug tips, pouring a stream across the fold into a glass waiting on the flat half. Lower it to stop. But the stream is still falling, so the trick is to stop just before the line.

No ads. No in-app purchases. No accounts. No data collected. Pay once and it's all yours.

MADE FOR THE FOLD. PLAYS ON EVERY iPhone.
On iPhone Duo, the hinge is the only control. The glass stays still on the table while the jug half moves, and you pour by feel with slow, gentle lifts. You never need to close the phone or fold fast. On any other iPhone, drag up anywhere to tip the jug and let go to set it upright. Same glasses, same physics, same leaderboards.

POURING THAT FEELS TRUE
• The drink in the jug stays level, so a full jug pours at a slight tip and a nearly empty one needs a steep one
• The stream takes time to fall: stop early, or watch it sail past the line
• The glass sings as it fills. The pitch rises, so you can pour by ear
• Glugs you can feel, surfaces that wobble, foam that climbs and settles, and a bright ting on every Perfect

FIVE VENUES, ONE SHIFT AT A TIME
• Lemonade Stand: water, lemonade and orange juice, from tumblers to flutes
• Soda Fountain: foam. Pour slowly, then top up
• Milkshake Diner: thick shakes, honey and syrup that keep coming after you stop
• The Conveyor: glasses that won't wait for you
• Potion Shop: tiny vials, millilitre marks and lines that fade
Earn stars to open the next venue. Collect enough to find out what's behind the counter.

RUSH
One big jug and glasses that keep coming. Every Perfect tops the jug up and grows your multiplier, all the way to ×5. Three spills, or an empty jug, and the run is over. Chase your best on the Game Center leaderboard.

DAILY POUR
Ten glasses, the same for everyone today, and one scored try. Then share your row of results without giving the glasses away.

CALLED TO THE DROP
Every glass gets a word: Perfect, Great, Good, Short, Over or Spill. Protect your Perfect streak, collect stars and watch your lifetime stats grow: litres poured, Perfects, best streak.

GAME CENTER
Leaderboards for Rush and the Daily Pour, and ten achievements. It's optional: Brim works fully without signing in.

SOUND AND FEEL
Every sound is synthesised in the app as you pour. There are no recordings. Sound and haptics each switch off in Settings. Reduce Motion turns off screen shake and thins out the particles.

EVERY DRINK IS NON-ALCOHOLIC
Lemonade, juice, sodas, shakes, syrups and potions (the fizzy, colourful, entirely made-up kind).

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No accounts, no tracking, no data collected. Your progress stays on your iPhone.

review.notes:
Thanks for reviewing Brim: a paid game with no ads, no in-app purchases, no accounts, no data collection and no network requests of its own.

1. ANY iPHONE (start here)
You don't need a Duo. Every mode, venue, unlock and achievement works on any iPhone and in the Simulator.
- Tap Play. A jug sits at the top, a glass with a fill line on the counter below.
- Drag UP anywhere: the jug tips and pours. Let go: it eases upright and the pour stops.
- The stream takes a moment to fall, so stop just before the line. Each glass is judged Perfect / Great / Good / Short / Over (too full) / Spill (over the rim).

2. iPHONE DUO (hinge)
The hinge angle comes only from the public iOS 27.1 API (SwiftUI onHingeChange). No private API.
a) Upside down by default: as a fold starts, iOS blurs one physical half of the inner display for about 2 s (all apps), so Brim runs the inner screen upside down to keep the glasses on the half that stays sharp. If the game looks upside down, turn the phone round once (hold it up for a second so iOS turns too). Settings > Controls > "Glasses on the sharp half" (Duo only) switches this off and restores the usual orientation. A one-time card on Home explains it.
b) Lay the Duo open on a table, inner screen up, fold running left to right: jug on the far half, glass on the near half. "Lay it flat to start" opens at about 168 degrees; after 6 s it also offers "Use touch instead".
c) Lift the far half like a laptop lid: the jug tips and pours across the fold. Nothing pours until the lid is about 6 degrees up. Lower it to stop. Play stays between about 174 and 90 degrees, with slow, held angles.
d) Book pose (fold top to bottom): the game pauses with "Turn me so the fold runs side to side, then lay me flat." and a "Use touch" button, which plays on the right-hand page, clear of the fold.
e) Below about 70 degrees a run pauses and nothing is judged; it resumes once open and flat. Closed, the outer display shows a status card (it says when a run is paused); "Pour here with touch" plays there, and opening the phone returns to the hinge behind "Lay it flat to carry on".
f) Split View, or any window smaller than the inner display: Brim uses touch (drag up), as on other iPhones. Windows too small to pour in show "Make Brim full screen to pour".
g) Settings > Controls > "Touch controls on iPhone Duo" uses drag full time.

3. KIND TO THE DEVICE (Guidelines 2.4.2, 1.4.5)
- Brim never asks the user to close the phone or fold quickly or repeatedly. The hinge is a slow dial, read by angle, never by the closed state.
- Nothing is placed on or between the screens.
- Nothing rewards folding speed or fold count; flapping the lid only spills drinks.

4. MODES AND UNLOCKS (nothing hidden, nothing to buy)
- Shifts: five venues (Lemonade Stand, Soda Fountain, Milkshake Diner, The Conveyor, Potion Shop). Stars open the next venue.
- A sixth, secret venue (Sand Bar) opens at 105 of the 120 stars in the five main venues. No code, shortcut or purchase.
- Rush: endless; ends after 3 spills or when the jug runs dry. Quitting from the pause menu keeps the score.
- Daily Pour: 10 glasses, the same for everyone, new each day at 00:00 UTC; one scored attempt (leaving part-way keeps the score so far), then unscored practice. The result can be shared as text via the share sheet.

5. CONTENT
Every drink is non-alcoholic: water, lemonade, juice, sodas, milkshakes, honey, syrup and fictional potions. A spill makes a puddle; nothing is harmed.

6. PRIVACY
No third-party SDKs, analytics, ads or tracking. Progress stays on the device. Data Not Collected.

7. GAME CENTER
Optional. 2 leaderboards (Rush, Daily Pour) and 10 achievements (700 points, 1 hidden). Brim works fully when not signed in.

8. OTHER
- No notifications, no rating prompt.
- Sound plays in Silent Mode (playback, mixes with other audio); Settings > "Respect silent mode" turns that off.
- Debug and demo modes are disabled in Release builds.

nomination.name: Brim - App Launch - iPhone Duo fold-to-pour game
nomination.description:
Brim makes iPhone Duo the jug. Lay the Duo open in tabletop pose and lift the top half like a laptop lid: a jug drawn on that half tips with it, and a stream pours across the fold into a glass on the flat half. Lower it to stop, but the stream is still falling, so the skill is stopping just before the line.

The hinge is an analogue control, not a switch. The liquid in the jug stays level, so a full jug pours at a slight lift and an empty one needs a steep one. The pitch rises as the glass fills, so players learn to pour by ear. Soda foams, milkshakes keep coming, potions demand precision.

Five venues of shifts, an endless Rush mode with a Perfect-streak multiplier, and a seeded Daily Pour that is the same for everyone and shares as a row of emoji, with Game Center leaderboards.

Every iPhone can play by dragging up. One price, no ads, no in-app purchases, no data collected, and every drink is non-alcoholic.
nomination.notes: Optimized for iPhone Duo, in every pose: hinge play in tabletop pose on the inner display, a turn card or touch play in book pose, touch play in Split View, and a status card on the outer display. It runs upside down by default so the fold blur misses the glasses. Uses the public iOS 27.1 hinge API with slow, held angles between flat and upright; it never asks players to close the phone or fold fast. Every sound is synthesized in the app. Also from us: Squish (launching 24 Nov).
